title: dev-ex-api-skeleton-and-ide-snippets-wip
content:
Status: Draft -- snapshot notes and minimal runnable examples for a fast first dev loop

Goal
- Ship a tiny, language-agnostic API skeleton + IDE snippets that let an engineer get a tokenized echo + streaming response working in under 10 minutes.
- Reduce cognitive load: provide the smallest set of files to clone, run, and iterate with Redwood Hosted API and the local stub runner.
- Surface telemetry and error-handling patterns so teams adopt consistent instrumentation from day 1.

Audience
- Product engineers building prototypes and internal demos
- Solutions engineers who need reproducible examples for PoCs
- Developer advocates creating workshops and live-coding sessions

Non-goals
- Full-featured SDK with all languages. Focus on 2 primary reference paths: Node (TypeScript) and Python.
- Opinionated state management, UI components, or production orchestration. Keep examples minimal, composable.

Design principles- Minimal files: one config, one sample app file, one README- Explicit but small: show network call, streaming handler, error path, retry sketch- Local-first: include a hermetic local stub that mimics streaming behavior and KV caching hints- Instrumented by default: include telemetry events and a tiny contract for logs/metrics

What to include (MVP)
1) repo-layout (single folder):
   - config.example.json  (apiKey placeholder, model selection, streaming=true)
   - README.md (10-minute path + troubleshooting)
   - ts/sample-app.ts or py/sample_app.py (single-file app)
   - local-stub/{server.js or server.py} (mocks streaming chunks + delay)
   - telemetry-contract.md (list of events + examples)
   - quick-start.sh (one-liner to run the sample end-to-end)

2) IDE snippets pack (VS Code):
   - code actions: import client, start stream handler, insert retry helper
   - workspace settings: recommended extensions (redwood-sdk-snippets, editorconfig)
   - sample launch config for 'Run Sample' that starts the stub then runs sample-app

3) Sample flows to demonstrate common patterns:
   - Echo + streaming: show progressive rendering in console
   - Function/tool calling: stubbed tool invocation and how to parse structured output
   - Retry and idempotency hints: exponential backoff, jitter example
   - Local dev cache hint: illustrate where to place prefix/KV cache and a no-op cache implementation

Telemetry contract (short)
- event: devx.sdk.request.start  (tags: language, sample, model, streaming=true/false)
- event: devx.sdk.request.chunk  (size_tokens, duration_ms, model_variant)
- event: devx.sdk.request.end    (status: success|error, total_tokens, latency_ms)
- event: devx.sdk.stub.fallback  (stub_name, reason)
- logs: sample-app writes structured logs to stdout with trace_id and request_id

Quickstart (10-minute path)
1) git clone ... && cd sample
2) cp config.example.json config.json && set API_KEY
3) ./quick-start.sh  (starts stub -> runs sample -> prints streaming output)
4) Inspect telemetry: open ./tmp/telemetry.log or use local collector command

Sample Node snippet (pseudocode)
- start stream: client.generate({model, prompt, stream:true})
- client.on('token', (t) => process.stdout.write(t))
- client.on('error', (e) => console.error('request failed', e))
- finally emit event devx.sdk.request.end

Developer experience notes (observations and open items)
- Many users get stuck on "how to render streaming in a terminal". Include two small render helpers: "plain console" and "progressive HTML fragment".
- Telemetry contract needs a compact JSON schema (1 page) that can be copy-pasted into customers' dashboards.
- Local stub should intentionally simulate 3 failure modes: partial stream drop, delayed KV cache miss, and small token-level corruption to exercise parsing robustness.

Checklist (owner / ETA)
- Write sample-app.ts and sample_app.py (owner: Diego Ramirez) - ETA: 2024-11-22
- Build stub server with chunked responses (owner: Sana Chopra) - ETA: 2024-11-12 (prototype done)
- Create VS Code snippets and launch config (owner: Liam O'Connor) - ETA: 2024-11-18
- Draft telemetry_contract.md and example dashboards (owner: Aisha K. Patel) - ETA: 2024-11-20
- Quick-start script and CI smoke job (owner: Diego) - ETA: 2024-11-25

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- A new user can follow README and have streaming echo + telemetry file within 10 minutes on Mac/Linux
- Sample supports both real Hosted API (with apiKey) and local stub with single switch in config.json
- Telemetry file is small JSON-lines and contains the events in the contract
- CI smoke test runs the stub and verifies that a streaming session completed and telemetry events were recorded

Open questions / risks
- Which default model do we set in examples? Recommendation: x1-medium (cost-conscious) but allow explicit override
- Do we include a browser example in MVP? Pros: better for demos. Cons: increases complexity (CORS, bundling). Defer to v1 if needed.
- Should the quick-start auto-open a small web UI? avoid for MVP, opt-in with --ui flag.

Notes to self / TODOs (rough)
- Add short GIF showing terminal streaming to README (owner: Liam)
- Link to devtools console recipe for capturing token-level latency (owner: Aisha)
- Coordinate with docs team to include the snippets package in the central docs sidebar (ticket: DOCS-314)

References / inspiration
- internal: confluence/team/DEVX/api-skeleton-brief
- external: small examples from popular SDKs but keep license-free text

Next steps
- Merge a tiny PR with just the Node sample + README so we can user-test in next "office hours" session.
- Collect live feedback from 5 early adopters (engineers + solutions leads) and iterate on the telemetry schema and stub failure modes.

-- end snapshot --

Unresolved: add concrete linting rules for code samples (prettier/eslint config), decide on allowed external deps, and finalize names for telemetry events (consistent prefix).
